Give up: this segmentation cannot express 4 of the 9 real bends at 80% coverage or better.

The part has 9 bends:
- 2 V bottoms at the arm top ends: 8-12 and 10-11
- 2 folds from plate to slope at the arm top ends
- 2 lips at the arm bottom ends: 13/15 and 14/17
- 1 tab root: 4/5
- 2 joggle folds: 1-7 and 3-7

Patches 18 (thickness strip) and 19 (noise) are not bends.

Root cause: plate patches 1 and 2 are each one global plane over the whole 487 x 236 mm sheet. The arms are slightly warped, so near the arm ends the plate skin sits 0.3-1.5 mm off those planes (left arm median about 0.8-1.0 mm). When `lines` relabels the full-resolution points, it drops any point more than 0.413 mm from its patch's global plane (assign_full_resolution, gate = min(0.6, 0.45t)). That strips the plate support next to these folds. The grey diagonal regions in closeup_B3, B5 and B6 show exactly this.

I replayed compute_bend with the same gate on points_ds.npz (read-only, scratchpad script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-idantal/db065cf7-f766-4885-b217-ed8d7edd7ade/scratchpad/sim_lines_186.py). It reproduced the current run: 2-9 fails; 1-10 short; 2-13 3.8 mm against 4.1 actual; 2-14 9.4 against 9.4; 2-4 16.1 against 15.9; 8-12, 10-11, 1-7 and 3-7 match.

Gated plate coverage along each problem fold:
- Left arm top fold: 0% on both skins. 1-8, 2-8, 1-9 and 2-9 all fail.
- Right arm top fold: patch 1 13%, patch 2 absent. 2-10 fails.
- Left arm bottom lip: 0% on both skins.
- Right arm bottom lip: 41% (patch 2) and 31% (patch 1). Best line is 11 mm.

So the verifiers' fixes 1-8, 2-10, 1-15/2-15 and 1-17/2-17 would still fail or stay short. Even the maximum 0.6 mm gate leaves both left-arm folds at 0%. No other patch lies on the arm plates, so no pair and no side made of several coplanar patches can fix this.

The 5 bends that can be expressed all land: 8-12, 10-11, 1-5 (replaces 2-4, 78.9 mm), 1-7 and 3-7.

To fix: re-prep so each arm end gets its own local plate patch, or change `lines` to gate against a local plane.

Part 23553000 has 16 real formed bends: 4 legs (90 deg root, then about 59 deg, then about 118 deg foot folds), a 90 deg end flange, a 90 deg tab bent down from a window, and a two-fold offset tab. I checked all 12 existing lines (B2, B3, B7-B16) in their closeups; each sits on the fold apex and covers about 90-97% of the fold.

The other 4 are real 90 deg folds with no line: 1-3, 1-9, 1-11 and 1-16. Measured against a plate plane fitted next to each fold (rms 0.006-0.024 mm), they give 89.6-89.9 deg, and the scanned bend arc is continuous over 100% of each fold. The apex offset is 1.0-1.16 mm, the same signature as the accepted B2 and B3.

The current segmentation cannot express these 4 in a form the line tool can compute. The plate is a single planar patch on each skin (patches 1 and 2), but the sheet is bowed about 3 mm along its 452 mm length: rms 0.92 mm, against 0.006-0.04 mm for every other patch. Residuals to the global plane are about -1.0 to -1.1 mm at the tab-16 fold, and +0.9 to +1.9 mm in magnitude at legs 9 and 11 and at the end flange. The full-resolution label step (lines.assign_full_resolution) drops every point more than 0.42 mm from its patch's global plane, so at these four folds the plate side has no usable points on either skin.

I emulated compute_bend read-only on the prep's downsampled points. It reproduces the run exactly: the same 12 lines succeed with the same angles and coverages (B2 0.62, B3 0.00), and 1-3, 1-9, 1-11 and 1-16 fail with the same errors. No pair from this prep can produce these 4 lines, and writing only 12 would make an incomplete gold label.

To fix it, either re-run prep so the bowed plate splits into locally planar pieces, or gate plate points against a local plane near each fold. Without the gate, the same outer-skin pairs compute cleanly: 1-3 at 79.5 mm and 1-16 at 77.9 mm, both with coverage 1.0. Then re-run lines with the 16-pair list above. I kept the outer-skin pairs because the inner twin 2-12 covers only about 41 of 79 mm even without the gate.

The front and iso views clearly show a two-fold S-offset, not a gentle roll. I checked this read-only on points_ds.npz, using s along the long axis and h along the patch-1 normal, measured from the patch-1 centroid. The top skin is flat at h=0 for s=-10.5..10. Fold A is at s≈10..14 and is convex on the top skin, which is patches 1 and 2. A short sloped web sits at s≈13.6..16.6, about 3.5-4 mm along the slope. Fold B is at s≈16.5..19.5 and is convex on the bottom skin, which is patches 3 and 6. The surface is then flat at h=-3.8 for s=19.5..31.
